title: Relative Clauses with the Subjunctive: Laws and Crops That Do Not Exist Yet

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and the subjunctive from B2 Unit 13. If you can point at the thing, the verb after *que* is in the indicative; if the thing is only wanted, needed or imagined, or you say it does not exist, the verb goes into the subjunctive. Debates about the páramos are full of such things: laws, crops and guides that people ask for and that may not exist yet.

sections.title: Real, or not found yet?
rows: Piden leyes que protejan los páramos.
Existe una ley que protege los páramos.
No hay nadie que conozca todo el páramo.
Conozco a un guía que conoce el páramo.

items.spanish: Buscamos un guía que conozca bien el páramo de Chingaza.
items.english: We are looking for a guide who knows the Chingaza páramo well.

items.spanish: Los campesinos necesitan cultivos que no dañen el agua del páramo.
items.english: The farmers need crops that do not harm the water of the páramo.

items.spanish: En el páramo hay plantas que guardan el agua de la niebla.
items.english: In the páramo there are plants that store the water of the mist.

items.spanish: No existe ningún cultivo que no cambie el paisaje.
items.english: There is no crop that does not change the landscape.

sections.content: Ask one question: can I point at it? If you can name it, see it or hold it, use the indicative. If it is only wanted, needed or imagined, or if you say it does not exist, use the subjunctive. Keep the personal *a* before a person: *Busco a un guía que…*.
